finalText:
It's small — five files, one clear line through them.

**`server.js`** is the front door. Every request lands here, gets its login token checked, then goes to the router.

**`auth.js`** checks that token. It's a user id plus a signed code made with a shared secret — no database lookup needed to catch fakes.

**`routes.js`** is the list of things the app can do: get a user, list someone's orders, add an order.

**`cache.js`** is a small memory shelf holding the last 256 answers, so repeat reads skip the store.

**`store.js`** is the actual data, kept in memory rather than a real database. Anything unread for 15 minutes quietly disappears.

Reads flow through the shelf first. Writes (adding an order) skip it and go straight to the data, so the shelf never gets stale.

One thing worth flagging: there's no `package.json` or test files anywhere, so nothing here is wired up to run or verify yet.
